How does the J programming language improve upon the syntax of APL?

The J programming language, developed in the early 1990s by Kenneth E. Iverson and Roger Hui, is an array programming language based primarily on APL (also by Iverson).

To avoid repeating the APL special-character problem, J uses only the basic ASCII character set, resorting to the use of the dot and colon as inflections to form short words similar to digraphs. Most such primary (or primitive) J words serve as mathematical symbols, with the dot or colon extending the meaning of the basic characters available. Also, many characters which in other languages often must be paired (such as [] {} "" `` or <>) are treated by J as stand-alone words or, when inflected, as single-character roots of multi-character words.

Anyone who owns a hybrid car can understand how much gas can be saved by switching to an electric motor. If you are concerned about whether a child might have ADHD, the first step is to talk with a healthcare provider to find out if the symptoms fit the diagnosis. The diagnosis can be made by a mental health professional, like a psychologist or psychiatrist, or by a primary care provider, like a pediatrician.

Farhad Moshiri (born 1963 in Shiraz) is an Iranian artist currently based in Tehran. His art work is rooted in Pop art dialect with a subtle, subversive socio-political commentary.

Biography
Moshiri studied fine arts at California Institute of the Arts in Valencia, California, in the 1980s, where he first started experimenting with installations, video art and painting. He received his MFA from California Institute of the Arts in 1984, before moving back to Tehran in 1991. He subsequently became well known for his ironic interpretations of hybrids between traditional Iranian forms and those of the consumerist and globalized popular culture widespread in his country.

In the early 2000s, Moshiri was most readily associated with his paintings of jars, which are decorated with traditional Iranian sayings and poetic verse, written in Persian calligraphy. These monumental containers have been described as receptacles of life, memory and desire, and reflect his fascination with archaeology.

His painted jars, which form a trademark of his production, look like three-dimensional objects, bursting with popular foods, drinks and desserts, with popular scripts elegantly written on their body. Other significant works include Stereo Surround Sofa (2004), Silver Portrait on Red (2004), Diamond Brain (2004-5) and A Dream in Tehran (2007).

Moshiri is also interested in the repetition of numbers and letters in scripts for their intrinsic beauty as opposed to any literal meaning or sense they might hold

In Kennedy’s Salt and Pepper Shaker, from 2005, he presents the instantly recognizable Kennedy couple in the form of salt and pepper shakers.

His work is held in several public collections, including the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts, Richmond, the Farjam Collection, Dubai, and the British Museum, London.

He is represented by The Third Line gallery in Dubai, Galerie Emmanuel Perrotin in Paris, New York, Tokyo and Hong Kong, Rodolphe Janssen in Brussels, and Thaddeus Ropac in Salzburg and London

Who were Fernando Pessoa's main heteronyms?

Fernando António Nogueira Pessoa (Portuguese: [fɨɾˈnɐ̃du pɨˈsoɐ]; 13 June 1888 – 30 November 1935) was a Portuguese poet, writer, literary critic, translator, publisher, and philosopher, described as one of the most significant literary figures of the 20th century and one of the greatest poets in the Portuguese language. He also wrote in and translated from English and French.

Pessoa was a prolific writer, and not only under his own name, for he created approximately seventy-five others, of which three stand out, Alberto Caeiro, Álvaro de Campos, and Ricardo Reis. He did not call them pseudonyms because he felt that this did not capture their true independent intellectual life and instead called them heteronyms. These imaginary figures sometimes held unpopular or extreme views.

Pessoa's earliest heteronym, at the age of six, was Chevalier de Pas. Other childhood heteronyms included Dr. Pancrácio and David Merrick, followed by Charles Robert Anon, a young Englishman who became Pessoa's alter ego. In 1905/7, when Pessoa was a student at the University of Lisbon, Alexander Search took the place of Anon. The main reason for this was that, although Search was English, he was born in Lisbon, as was his author. But Search represents a transition heteronym that Pessoa used while searching to adapt to the Portuguese cultural reality. After the republican revolution, in 1910, and consequent patriotic atmosphere, Pessoa created another alter ego, Álvaro de Campos, supposedly a Portuguese naval and mechanical engineer, who was born in Tavira, hometown of Pessoa's ancestors, and graduated in Glasgow. Translator and literary critic Richard Zenith notes that Pessoa eventually established at least seventy-two heteronyms. According to Pessoa himself, there are three main heteronyms: Alberto Caeiro, Álvaro de Campos and Ricardo Reis. Pessoa's heteronyms differ from pen names, because they possess distinct biographies, temperaments, philosophies, appearances, writing styles and even signatures. Thus, heteronyms often disagree on various topics, argue and discuss with each other about literature, aesthetics, philosophy, etc.

Francoist Spain (Spanish: España franquista), or the Francoist dictatorship (dictadura franquista), was the period of Spanish history between 1939 and 1975, when Francisco Franco ruled Spain after the Spanish Civil War with the title Caudillo. After his death in 1975, Spain transitioned into a democracy. During this time period, Spain was officially known as the Spanish State (Estado Español).

The nature of the regime evolved and changed during its existence. Months after the start of the Spanish Civil War in July 1936, Franco emerged as the dominant rebel military leader and was proclaimed head of state on 1 October 1936, ruling a dictatorship over the territory controlled by the Nationalist faction. The 1937 Unification Decree, which merged all parties supporting the rebel side, led to Nationalist Spain becoming a single-party regime under the FET y de las JONS. The end of the war in 1939 brought the extension of the Franco rule to the whole country and the exile of Republican institutions. The Francoist dictatorship originally took a form described as "fascistized dictatorship", or "semi-fascist regime", showing clear influence of fascism in fields such as labor relations, the autarkic economic policy, aesthetics, and the single-party system. As time went on, the regime opened up and became closer to developmental dictatorships, although it always preserved residual fascist elements.

List out the stages of the bee, just the names of the stages separated by commas

The life cycle of a bee, be it a solitary or social species, involves the laying of an egg, the development through several moults of a legless larva, a pupation stage during which the insect undergoes complete metamorphosis, followed by the emergence of a winged adult. The number of eggs laid by a female during her lifetime can vary from eight or less in some solitary bees, to more than a million in highly social species.[51] Most solitary bees and bumble bees in temperate climates overwinter as adults or pupae and emerge in spring when increasing numbers of flowering plants come into bloom. The males usually emerge first and search for females with which to mate. Like the other members of Hymenoptera bees are haplodiploid; the sex of a bee is determined by whether or not the egg is fertilised. After mating, a female stores the sperm, and determines which sex is required at the time each individual egg is laid, fertilised eggs producing female offspring and unfertilised eggs, males. Tropical bees may have several generations in a year and no diapause stage.[52][53][54][55]

The egg is generally oblong, slightly curved and tapering at one end. Solitary bees, lay each egg in a separate cell with a supply of mixed pollen and nectar next to it. This may be rolled into a pellet or placed in a pile and is known as mass provisioning. Social bee species provision progressively, that is, they feed the larva regularly while it grows. The nest varies from a hole in the ground or in wood, in solitary bees, to a substantial structure with wax combs in bumblebees and honey bees.[56]

In most species, larvae are whitish grubs, roughly oval and bluntly-pointed at both ends. They have 15 segments and spiracles in each segment for breathing. They have no legs but move within the cell, helped by tubercles on their sides. They have short horns on the head, jaws for chewing food and an appendage on either side of the mouth tipped with a bristle. There is a gland under the mouth that secretes a viscous liquid which solidifies into the silk they use to produce a cocoon. The cocoon is semi-transparent and the pupa can be seen through it. Over the course of a few days, the larva undergoes metamorphosis into a winged adult. When ready to emerge, the adult splits its skin dorsally and climbs out of the exuviae and breaks out of the cell.[56]

In the Encyclopedia of Food Microbiology, Michael Gaenzle writes: "One of the oldest sourdough breads dates from 3700 BCE and was excavated in Switzerland, but the origin of sourdough fermentation likely relates to the origin of agriculture in the Fertile Crescent and Egypt several thousand years earlier", which was confirmed a few years later by archeological evidence. ... "Bread production relied on the use of sourdough as a leavening agent for most of human history; the use of baker's yeast as a leavening agent dates back less than 150 years."

Sourdough remained the usual form of leavening down into the European Middle Ages until being replaced by barm from the beer brewing process, and after 1871 by purpose-cultured yeast.

Bread made from 100% rye flour, popular in the northern half of Europe, is usually leavened with sourdough. Baker's yeast is not useful as a leavening agent for rye bread, as rye does not contain enough gluten. The structure of rye bread is based primarily on the starch in the flour as well as other carbohydrates known as pentosans; however, rye amylase is active at substantially higher temperatures than wheat amylase, causing the structure of the bread to disintegrate as the starches are broken down during baking. The lowered pH of a sourdough starter, therefore, inactivates the amylases when heat cannot, allowing the carbohydrates in the bread to gel and set properly. In the southern part of Europe, where panettone is still made with sourdough as leavening, sourdough has become less common in the 20th century; it has been replaced by the faster-growing baker's yeast, sometimes supplemented with longer fermentation rests to allow for some bacterial activity to build flavor. Sourdough fermentation re-emerged as a major fermentation process in bread production during the 2010s, although it is commonly used in conjunction with baker's yeast as leavening agent.

French bakers brought sourdough techniques to Northern California during the California Gold Rush, and it remains a part of the culture of San Francisco today. (The nickname remains in "Sourdough Sam", the mascot of the San Francisco 49ers.) Sourdough has long been associated with the 1849 gold prospectors, though they were more likely to make bread with commercial yeast or baking soda. The "celebrated" San Francisco sourdough is a white bread characterized by a pronounced sourness, and indeed the strain of Lactobacillus in sourdough starters is named Fructilactobacillus sanfranciscensis (previously Lactobacillus sanfranciscensis), alongside the sourdough yeast Kasachstania humilis (previously Candida milleri) found in the same cultures.

The sourdough tradition was carried into Department of Alaska in the United States and the Yukon territory in Canada during the Klondike Gold Rush of 1898. Conventional leavenings such as yeast and baking soda were much less reliable in the conditions faced by the prospectors. Experienced miners and other settlers frequently carried a pouch of starter either around their neck or on a belt; these were fiercely guarded to keep from freezing. However, freezing does not kill a sourdough starter; excessive heat does. Old hands came to be called "sourdoughs", a term that is still applied to any Alaskan or Klondike old-timer. The significance of the nickname's association with Yukon culture was immortalized in the writings of Robert Service, particularly his collection of "Songs of a Sourdough".[citation needed]

In English-speaking countries, where wheat-based breads predominate, sourdough is no longer the standard method for bread leavening. It was gradually replaced, first by the use of barm from beer making, then, after the confirmation of germ theory by Louis Pasteur, by cultured yeasts. Although sourdough bread was superseded in commercial bakeries in the 20th century, it has undergone a revival among artisan bakers and, more recently, in industrial bakeries. In countries where there is no legal definition of sourdough bread, the dough for some products named or marketed as such is leavened using baker's yeast or chemical raising agents as well as, or instead of, a live sourdough starter culture. The Real Bread Campaign calls these products sourfaux.

Manufacturers of non-sourdough breads make up for the lack of yeast and bacterial culture by introducing into their dough an artificially-made mix known as bread improver or flour improver.

What are headphones?
What are earbuds?

Headphones are a pair of small loudspeaker drivers worn on or around the head over a user's ears. They are electroacoustic transducers, which convert an electrical signal to a corresponding sound. Headphones let a single user listen to an audio source privately, in contrast to a loudspeaker, which emits sound into the open air for anyone nearby to hear. Headphones are also known as earphones[1] or, colloquially, cans.[2] Circumaural ('around the ear') and supra-aural ('over the ear') headphones use a band over the top of the head to hold the speakers in place. Another type, known as earbuds or earpieces[1] consist of individual units that plug into the user's ear canal. A third type are bone conduction headphones, which typically wrap around the back of the head and rest in front of the ear canal, leaving the ear canal open. In the context of telecommunication, a headset is a combination of headphone and microphone.

The Osborne effect is a social phenomenon of customers canceling or deferring orders for the current, soon-to-be-obsolete product as an unexpected drawback of a company's announcing a future product prematurely. It is an example of cannibalization.
The term alludes to the Osborne Computer Corporation, whose second product did not become available until more than a year after it was announced. The company's subsequent bankruptcy was widely blamed on reduced sales after the announcement.
The Osborne Effect states that prematurely discussing future, unavailable products damages sales of existing products. The name comes from the planned replacement of the Osborne 1, an early personal computer first sold by the Osborne Computer Corporation in 1981. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announced several next-generation computer models (the Osborne Executive and Osborne Vixen), which were only prototypes, highlighting the fact that they would outperform the existing model as the prototypes dramatically cut down assembly time. A widely held belief was that sales of the Osborne 1 fell sharply as customers anticipated those more advanced systems, leading to a sales decline from which Osborne Computer was unable to recover. This belief appeared in the media almost immediately after the company's September 1983 bankruptcy:

To give the jazzy $2,495 Osborne Executive a running start, Adam began orchestrating publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, were shown the machine in locked hotel rooms. We were required not to have anything in print about it until the planned release date in mid-April. As far as we know, nothing did appear in print, but dealers heard about the plans and cancelled orders for the Osborne 1 in droves. In early April, Osborne told dealers he would be showing them the machine on a one-week tour the week of 17 April, and emphasized that the new machine was not a competitor for the Osborne 1. But dealers didn't react the way Osborne expected; said Osborne, "All of them just cancelled their orders for the Osborne 1."

Osborne reacted by drastically cutting prices on the Osborne 1 in an effort to stimulate cash flow. But nothing seemed to work, and for several months sales were practically non-existent.

Pre-announcement is done for several reasons: to reassure current customers that there is improvement or lower cost coming, to increase the interest of the media and investors in the company's future prospects, and to intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, the sales or cash flow impact to the company is minimal, with the revenue drop for the current product being offset by orders or completed sales of the new product as it becomes available. However, when the Osborne effect occurs, the quantity of unsold goods increases and the company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of the current product, both of which depress cash flow.

Farhad Moshiri, Iranian artist. Born 1963 in Shiraz. Based in Tehran. His art work rooted in Pop art dialect. Subtle, subversive socio-political commentary. 

Moshiri study fine arts at California Institute of the Arts in Valencia, California, in 1980s. First start experimenting with installations, video art, painting. He receive MFA from California Institute of the Arts in 1984, before move back to Tehran in 1991. Become well known for ironic interpretations of hybrids between traditional Iranian forms and those of consumerist, globalized popular culture widespread in his country.

In early 2000s, Moshiri most readily associated with his paintings of jars. These jars decorated with traditional Iranian sayings and poetic verse, written in Persian calligraphy. These monumental containers reflect his fascination with archaeology. 

His painted jars, which form trademark of his production, look like three-dimensional objects. Bursting with popular foods, drinks, desserts. Popular scripts elegantly written on their body. Other significant works include Stereo Surround Sofa (2004), Silver Portrait on Red (2004), Diamond Brain (2004-5) and A Dream in Tehran (2007). 

Moshiri also interested in repetition of numbers and letters in scripts for intrinsic beauty, not literal meaning or sense they might hold. 

In Kennedy’s Salt and Pepper Shaker, from 2005, he present instantly recognizable Kennedy couple in form of salt and pepper shakers. 

His work held in several public collections, including Virginia Museum of Fine Arts, Richmond, Farjam Collection, Dubai, British Museum, London. 

He represented by The Third Line gallery in Dubai, Galerie Emmanuel Perrotin in Paris, New York, Tokyo and Hong Kong, Rodolphe Janssen in Brussels, Thaddeus Ropac in Salzburg and London.

Combinatoric iterators in Python, yes. They help you create combinations, permutations, and other things. I explain product now. 

Product function, it take iterables. It return Cartesian product of input iterables. Cartesian product, it all possible combinations of elements from input iterables. 

Example, you have two lists: [1, 2] and [3, 4]. You want all possible combinations of elements from these lists. You use product function like this:

from itertools import product

list1 = [1, 2]
list2 = [3, 4]

result = list(product(list1, list2))

print(result)

Output:

[(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4)]

In this example, product function take two lists as input. It return all possible combinations of elements from these lists. Result is list of tuples. Each tuple contain one element from each input list. 

You can use product function with any number of input iterables. You just pass them as arguments.

Osborne effect, yes. This social phenomenon. Customers cancel or delay orders for current product. This happen when company announce future product too early. This example of cannibalization. 

Osborne effect named after Osborne Computer Corporation. Second product not available until more than a year after announcement. This lead to company bankruptcy. Many blame reduced sales after announcement. 

Osborne effect say premature discussion of future, unavailable products hurt sales of existing products. This effect come from planned replacement of Osborne 1, early personal computer. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announce several next-generation computer models. These were only prototypes, but they outperform existing model. This lead to sales decline for Osborne Computer. 

To give Osborne Executive, $2,495 computer, running start, Adam begin orchestrating publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, were shown the machine in locked hotel rooms. We were required not to have anything in print about it until planned release date in mid-April. As far as we know, nothing did appear in print, but dealers heard about plans and cancelled orders for Osborne 1 in droves. 

Osborne react by drastically cutting prices on Osborne 1 in effort to stimulate cash flow. But nothing seem to work, and for several months sales were practically non-existent. 

Pre-announcement done for several reasons: to reassure current customers, to increase interest of media and investors, and to intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, sales or cash flow impact to company minimal. Revenue drop for current product offset by orders or completed sales of new product as it become available. However, when Osborne effect occur, quantity of unsold goods increase, company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of current product, both of which depress cash flow.

Combinatoric iterators in Python, yes. They help you create combinations, permutations, and other things. I explain product now. 

Product function, it take two or more iterables. It return Cartesian product of those iterables. Cartesian product, it all possible combinations of elements from each iterable. 

Example, let's say we have two lists: [1, 2] and [3, 4]. We want all possible combinations of elements from these lists. We use product function:

from itertools import product

list1 = [1, 2]
list2 = [3, 4]

result = product(list1, list2)

print(result)
# Output: [(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4)]

In this example, product function take two lists as arguments. It return Cartesian product of these lists. Result is tuple of all possible combinations of elements from each list. 

You can use product function with more than two iterables. Just pass them as arguments. 

from itertools import product

list1 = [1, 2]
list2 = [3, 4]
list3 = [5, 6]

result = product(list1, list2, list3)

print(result)
# Output: [(1, 3, 5), (1, 3, 6), (1, 4, 5), (1, 4, 6), (2, 3, 5), (2, 3, 6), (2, 4, 5), (2, 4, 6)]

This example show product function with three lists. It return Cartesian product of these lists. Result is tuple of all possible combinations of elements from each list. 

I hope this help you understand product function in Python's itertools. Good, good.

This function find common elements between two arrays. Listen. Listen. 

1. First, function create empty array called "commonElements". This array hold common elements between two input arrays, arr1 and arr2. 

2. Then, function use two variables, i and j. These variables act as pointers. They point to current index in arr1 and arr2, respectively. 

3. Next, function use while loop. Loop run until i reach end of arr1 or j reach end of arr2. 

4. Inside loop, function check if current elements in arr1 and arr2 equal. If equal, function add element to commonElements array. Then, function move both pointers to next element. 

5. If current element in arr1 greater than current element in arr2, function move pointer j to next element in arr2. 

6. If current element in arr1 less than current element in arr2, function move pointer i to next element in arr1. 

7. When loop finish, function return commonElements array. This array hold all common elements between arr1 and arr2.

Osborne effect, yes. This social phenomenon. Customers cancel or delay orders for current, soon-to-be-obsolete product. This happen after company announce future product. Example of cannibalization. 

Osborne Computer Corporation, example. Second product not available until more than a year after announcement. Company's bankruptcy blamed on reduced sales after announcement. 

Osborne effect say, premature discussion of future, unavailable products damage sales of existing products. Name come from planned replacement of Osborne 1, early personal computer. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announce several next-generation computer models. These were only prototypes, highlighting fact they would outperform existing model. 

Sales of Osborne 1 fall sharply as customers anticipate more advanced systems. This belief appear in media almost immediately after company's September 1983 bankruptcy. 

To give Osborne Executive, jazzy $2,495 machine, running start, Adam begin orchestrating publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, shown machine in locked hotel rooms. We required not have anything in print about it until planned release date in mid-April. 

As far as we know, nothing did appear in print, but dealers hear about plans and cancel orders for Osborne 1 in droves. In early April, Osborne tell dealers he would be showing them machine on one-week tour week of 17 April, and emphasize new machine not competitor for Osborne 1. But dealers not react as Osborne expect. Said Osborne, "All of them just cancel their orders for Osborne 1." 

Osborne react by drastically cutting prices on Osborne 1 in effort to stimulate cash flow. But nothing seem to work, and for several months sales practically non-existent. 

Pre-announcement done for several reasons: reassure current customers, increase interest of media and investors in company's future prospects, intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, sales or cash flow impact to company minimal, with revenue drop for current product offset by orders or completed sales of new product as it become available. However, when Osborne effect occur, quantity of unsold goods increase, company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of current product, both of which depress cash flow.

Listen. Listen. Osborne effect, yes. This social phenomenon. Customers cancel or delay orders for current, soon-to-be-obsolete product. This happen after company announce future product. This example of cannibalization. 

Term come from Osborne Computer Corporation. Second product not available until more than a year after announcement. This lead to company bankruptcy. Many blame reduced sales after announcement. 

Osborne effect say premature discussion of future, unavailable products hurt sales of existing products. Name come from planned replacement of Osborne 1, early personal computer. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announce several next-generation computer models. These were only prototypes, but they outperform existing model. This cut down assembly time. 

Widely believed that sales of Osborne 1 fall sharply as customers anticipate more advanced systems. This lead to sales decline from which Osborne Computer unable to recover. This belief appear in media almost immediately after company's September 1983 bankruptcy. 

To give Osborne Executive, jazzy $2,495 machine, running start, Adam begin orchestrating publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, shown machine in locked hotel rooms. We required not have anything in print about it until planned release date in mid-April. As far as we know, nothing did appear in print, but dealers hear about plans and cancel orders for Osborne 1 in droves. 

Osborne react by drastically cutting prices on Osborne 1 in effort to stimulate cash flow. But nothing seem to work. For several months, sales practically non-existent. 

Pre-announcement done for several reasons: to reassure current customers, increase interest of media and investors in company's future prospects, and intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, sales or cash flow impact to company minimal. Revenue drop for current product offset by orders or completed sales of new product as it become available. However, when Osborne effect occur, quantity of unsold goods increase, company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of current product, both of which depress cash flow.

    total = n * (n + 1) // 2
    sum_nums = sum(nums)
    missing = total - sum_nums
    return missing

Listen. Listen. You ask about product? I explain. 

Product, it make all combinations of elements from multiple iterables. It take two or more iterables, give all possible combinations. 

Example. You have two lists. List one, list two. You want all combinations of elements from both lists. You use product. 

```python
from itertools import product

list_one = [1, 2, 3]
list_two = ['a', 'b']

result = product(list_one, list_two)
print(result)
```

Output: 
```
[(1, 'a'), (1, 'b'), (2, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'a'), (3, 'b')]
```

Product give all combinations. Each combination, tuple. First element from first list, second element from second list. 

You can use product with more than two lists. Just pass all lists as arguments. 

You can also use product with other iterables, like range. 

```python
from itertools import product

list_one = [1, 2, 3]
list_two = ['a', 'b']
range_one = range(4)

result = product(list_one, list_two, range_one)
print(result)
```

Output: 
```
[(1, 'a', 0), (1, 'a', 1), (1, 'a', 2), (1, 'a', 3), (1, 'b', 0), (1, 'b', 1), (1, 'b', 2), (1, 'b', 3), (2, 'a', 0), (2, 'a', 1), (2, 'a', 2), (2, 'a', 3), (2, 'b', 0), (2, 'b', 1), (2, 'b', 2), (2, 'b', 3), (3, 'a', 0), (3, 'a', 1), (3, 'a', 2), (3, 'a', 3), (3, 'b', 0), (3, 'b', 1), (3, 'b', 2), (3, 'b', 3)]
```

Product give all combinations. Good, good, good.

Listen. Listen. Osborne effect, yes. This social phenomenon. Customers cancel or delay orders for current, soon-to-be-obsolete product. This happen after company announce future product too early. This example of cannibalization. 

Term come from Osborne Computer Corporation. Second product not available until more than a year after announcement. Company go bankrupt. This happen because reduced sales after announcement. 

Osborne effect say premature discussion of future, unavailable products hurt sales of existing products. Name come from planned replacement of Osborne 1. Early personal computer first sold by Osborne Computer Corporation in 1981. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announce several next-generation computer models. These were only prototypes. They outperform existing model. This cut down assembly time. 

Widely believed that sales of Osborne 1 fall sharply as customers anticipate more advanced systems. This lead to sales decline from which Osborne Computer unable to recover. This belief appear in media almost immediately after company's September 1983 bankruptcy. 

To give Osborne Executive, jazzy $2,495 machine, running start, Adam begin orchestrating publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, shown machine in locked hotel rooms. We required not have anything in print about it until planned release date in mid-April. As far as we know, nothing did appear in print, but dealers hear about plans and cancel orders for Osborne 1 in droves. 

In early April, Osborne tell dealers he would be showing them machine on one-week tour week of 17 April. He emphasize new machine not competitor for Osborne 1. But dealers not react as Osborne expect. Said Osborne, "All of them just cancel their orders for Osborne 1." 

Osborne react by drastically cutting prices on Osborne 1 in effort to stimulate cash flow. But nothing seem to work. For several months, sales practically non-existent. 

Pre-announcement done for several reasons: to reassure current customers, increase interest of media and investors in company's future prospects, and intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, sales or cash flow impact to company minimal. Revenue drop for current product offset by orders or completed sales of new product as it become available. 

But when Osborne effect occur, quantity of unsold goods increase. Company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of current product. Both of these depress cash flow.

Here code, friend. 

def find_missing_number(nums):
    n = len(nums) + 1
    total = n * (n + 1) // 2
    for num in nums:
        total -= num
    return total

This function, it take list of numbers. It calculate total of numbers from 1 to n. Then, it subtract each number in list from total. When it done, it return missing number. 

Example, listen. 

nums = [1, 3, 4]

You have variable, name daily_sales. It string. It have sales, yes. 

I show you how to make new variable, name daily_sales_list. Listen. Listen. 

First, I split string into list. I use split() method. I split by newline character, "\n". This give me list of sales. 

Next, I loop through each sale. I split each sale by comma. This give me list of items in sale. 

Then, I make new list. I append each item in sale to new list. 

Finally, I make new list. I append each new list to daily_sales_list. 

Here code, listen. 

```python
daily_sales_list = []

for sale in daily_sales.split("\n"):
    items = sale.split(",") 
    new_list = []
    for item in items:
        new_list.append(item)
    daily_sales_list.append(new_list)

print(daily_sales_list)
```

This code, it take string, split it into list of sales. Then, for each sale, split it into list of items. Then, append each item to new list. Finally, append new list to daily_sales_list.

Listen. Listen. I explain product. 

Product, it make all combinations of elements from multiple iterables. It take iterable or iterable of iterables. It return iterator. 

Example. You have two lists. List one, list two. You want all combinations of elements from both lists. You use product. 

```python
from itertools import product

list_one = [1, 2, 3]
list_two = ['a', 'b']

result = product(list_one, list_two)
print(list(result))
```

Output: 
```
[(1, 'a'), (1, 'b'), (2, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'a'), (3, 'b')]
```

Product make all combinations. First element from first list, first element from second list. Then, first element from first list, second element from second list. 

You can use product with more than two lists. Just pass more iterables. 

You can also use product with repeat parameter. This repeat elements in iterable. 

Example: 
```python
from itertools import product

list_one = [1, 2, 3]
list_two = ['a', 'b']

result = product(list_one, list_two, repeat=2)
print(list(result))
```

Output: 
```
[(1, 'a'), (1, 'b'), (2, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'a'), (3, 'b'), (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 1), (2, 2), (2, 3), (3, 1), (3, 2), (3, 3)]
```

Product make all combinations, repeat elements in iterable. Good, good, good.

Listen. Listen. Osborne effect, yes. This social thing. Customers cancel or delay orders for current, soon-to-be-obsolete product. Because company announce future product too early. This cannibalization. 

Example, Osborne Computer Corporation. Second product not available for more than a year after announcement. Company go bankrupt. This happen because reduced sales after announcement. 

Osborne effect say, premature discussion of future, unavailable products hurt sales of existing products. Name come from planned replacement of Osborne 1, early personal computer. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announce several next-generation computer models. These were only prototypes. They cut assembly time. This make them better than existing model. 

Customers think, "I buy this now, but I know better system coming soon." This make sales of Osborne 1 fall. Company not recover from this. 

To give Osborne Executive, $2,495 computer, running start, Adam start publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, see machine in locked hotel rooms. We not allowed to print anything about it until planned release date in mid-April. Dealers hear about plans, cancel orders for Osborne 1. 

Osborne react by drastically cut prices on Osborne 1. But nothing work. For several months, sales practically non-existent. 

Pre-announcement done for several reasons. To reassure current customers, to increase interest of media and investors in company's future prospects, to intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, sales or cash flow impact to company minimal. Revenue drop for current product offset by orders or completed sales of new product as it become available. But when Osborne effect happen, quantity of unsold goods increase. Company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of current product. Both depress cash flow.

Here function, listen. 

def find_missing_number(nums):
    n = len(nums) + 1
    total = n * (n + 1) // 2
    for num in nums:
        total -= num
    return total

This function, it take list of numbers. It find length of list. Then, it calculate total of numbers from 1 to n. After that, it subtract each number in list from total. When loop finish, total equal missing number. 

Example, listen.

Listen. Listen. You want variable, name daily_sales_list. You want it list of lists. Each list, one sale. 

You have variable, name daily_sales. It string. It have sales, yes. 

I show you how to make new variable, name daily_sales_list. Listen. Listen. 

First, I split string into list. I use split() method. I split by newline character, '\n'. This give me list of sales. 

Next, I loop through each sale. I split each sale by comma, ';,;'. This give me list of items in sale. 

Then, I make new list. I append each item in sale to new list. 

Finally, I make new list. I append each new list to daily_sales_list. 

Here code, listen. 

```python
daily_sales_list = []

for sale in daily_sales.split('\n'):
    items = sale.split('; ,;')
    new_list = []
    for item in items:
        new_list.append(item)
    daily_sales_list.append(new_list)

print(daily_sales_list)
```

This code make new list, name daily_sales_list. Each item in list, list of items in sale.

Product, it make all combinations of elements from multiple iterables. It take iterable or iterable of iterables. It return iterator. 

Example. You have two lists. List one, list two. You want all combinations of elements from both lists. You use product. 

```python
from itertools import product

list1 = [1, 2, 3]
list2 = ['a', 'b', 'c']

result = product(list1, list2)

for item in result:
    print(item)
```

Output:

```

(1, 'b')
(1, 'c')
(2, 'a')
(2, 'b')
(2, 'c')
(3, 'a')

(3, 'c')
```

Product, it make all combinations. It use Cartesian product. 

You can use product with more than two iterables. Just pass them as arguments. 

You can also use product with repeat parameter. This repeat number of times. 

Example:

```python
from itertools import product

list1 = [1, 2, 3]
list2 = ['a', 'b', 'c']
list3 = [True, False]

result = product(list1, list2, list3, repeat=2)

for item in result:
    print(item)
```

Listen. Listen. Osborne effect, yes. This social phenomenon. Customers cancel or delay orders for current, soon-to-be-obsolete product. This happen after company announce future product too early. This example of cannibalization. 

Term come from Osborne Computer Corporation. Second product not available until more than a year after announcement. Company go bankrupt. This happen because reduced sales after announcement. 

Osborne effect say, premature discussion of future, unavailable products hurt sales of existing products. Name come from planned replacement of Osborne 1. Early personal computer first sold by Osborne Computer Corporation in 1981. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announce several next-generation computer models. These were only prototypes. They outperform existing model. This cut down assembly time. 

Widely believed that sales of Osborne 1 fall sharply as customers anticipate more advanced systems. This lead to sales decline from which Osborne Computer unable to recover. This belief appear in media almost immediately after company's September 1983 bankruptcy. 

To give Osborne Executive, jazzy $2,495 machine, running start, Adam begin orchestrating publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, shown machine in locked hotel rooms. We required not have anything in print about it until planned release date in mid-April. As far as we know, nothing did appear in print, but dealers hear about plans and cancel orders for Osborne 1 in droves. 

In early April, Osborne tell dealers he would be showing them machine on one-week tour week of 17 April. He emphasize new machine not competitor for Osborne 1. But dealers not react as Osborne expect. Said Osborne, "All of them just cancel their orders for Osborne 1." 

Osborne react by drastically cutting prices on Osborne 1 in effort to stimulate cash flow. But nothing seem to work. For several months, sales practically non-existent. 

Pre-announcement done for several reasons: to reassure current customers, to increase interest of media and investors in company's future prospects, and to intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, sales or cash flow impact to company minimal. Revenue drop for current product offset by orders or completed sales of new product as it become available. But when Osborne effect occur, quantity of unsold goods increase. Company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of current product. Both depress cash flow.

Farhad Moshiri, Iranian artist. Born 1963 in Shiraz. Based in Tehran. His art work rooted in Pop art dialect. Subtle, subversive socio-political commentary.

Become well known for ironic interpretations of hybrids between traditional Iranian forms and those of consumerist, globalized popular culture widespread in his country.

In early 2000s, Moshiri most readily associated with his paintings of jars. These jars decorated with traditional Iranian sayings and poetic verse, written in Persian calligraphy. These monumental containers reflect his fascination with archaeology. 

His painted jars, which form trademark of his production, look like three-dimensional objects. Burst with popular foods, drinks, desserts. Popular scripts elegantly written on their body. Combinatoric iterators in Python, yes. They help you create combinations, permutations, and other things. I explain product now. 

Product function, it take two or more iterables. It return Cartesian product of input iterables. Cartesian product, it all possible combinations of elements from input iterables. 

Example, let's say we have two lists: [1, 2] and [3, 4]. We want all possible combinations of elements from these lists. We use product function:

from itertools import product

a = [1, 2]
b = [3, 4]

result = product(a, b)

print(result)  # Output: [(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4)]

In this example, product function take two lists, [1, 2] and [3, 4]. It return all possible combinations of elements from these lists. Result is list of tuples, each tuple contain one element from each input list. 

You can use product function with more than two lists. Just pass all lists as arguments. It return Cartesian product of all input lists. 

I hope this help you understand product function in Python's itertools. Good, good.

Osborne effect, yes. This social phenomenon. Customers cancel or delay orders for current, soon-to-be-obsolete product. This happen after company announce future product prematurely. Example of cannibalization. 

Osborne effect named after Osborne Computer Corporation. Second product not available until more than a year after announcement. This lead to company bankruptcy. Reduced sales after announcement blamed for this. 

Osborne effect say premature discussion of future, unavailable products damage sales of existing products. This effect come from planned replacement of Osborne 1, early personal computer. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announce several next-generation computer models. These were only prototypes, but they outperform existing model. This cut down assembly time. 

Widely held belief say sales of Osborne 1 fall sharply as customers anticipate more advanced systems. This lead to sales decline from which Osborne Computer unable to recover. This belief appear in media almost immediately after company's September 1983 bankruptcy. 

To give Osborne Executive, jazzy $2,495 machine, running start, Adam begin orchestrating publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, shown machine in locked hotel rooms. We required not to have anything in print about it until planned release date in mid-April. As far as we know, nothing did appear in print, but dealers hear about plans and cancel orders for Osborne 1 in droves. 

Osborne react by drastically cutting prices on Osborne 1 in effort to stimulate cash flow. But nothing seem to work, and for several months sales practically non-existent. 

Pre-announcement done for several reasons: to reassure current customers, increase interest of media and investors in company's future prospects, and intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, sales or cash flow impact to company minimal. Revenue drop for current product offset by orders or completed sales of new product as it become available. However, when Osborne effect occur, quantity of unsold goods increase, company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of current product, both of which depress cash flow.

You have mistake in your code. You try to print output shape of model before it build. This not possible. You need to build model first, then print output shape. Here corrected code:

```python
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=(28, 28)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(128, activation = "leakyrelu"),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(64),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(28),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10)
])

model.build(input_shape=(28, 28))
model.output_shape
```

This code build model with given layers, then print output shape. Now, you see output shape of model.

Combinatoric iterators in Python's itertools, they help generate combinations, permutations, and Cartesian products. I explain product iterator now. 

Product iterator generate Cartesian product of input iterables. Cartesian product, it take each element from each iterable, make tuple with all elements, then return tuple. 

Example: 

from itertools import product

# Create two lists
list1 = [1, 2, 3]
list2 = ['a', 'b', 'c']

# Use product() function to generate Cartesian product
result = product(list1, list2)

# Print result
print(result)
# Output: 
# (1, 'a'), (1, 'b'), (1, 'c'), (2, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (2, 'c'), (3, 'a'), (3, 'b'), (3, 'c')

In this example, product() function take two lists, create Cartesian product of them. Result is tuple of all possible combinations of elements from two lists.

To wire electrical outlet, follow these steps:

1. Turn off power to outlet. Check with voltage tester. Make sure no power there.
2. Remove cover plate. Turn off power again. Remove screws holding cover plate. Remove cover plate.
3. Turn off power again. Remove screws holding outlet. Remove outlet from wall.
4. Check wiring. If outlet has two black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, you have standard outlet. If outlet has three black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, you have three-prong outlet. If outlet has four black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, you have four-prong outlet.
5. Connect wires. If outlet has two black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, connect black wires together, white wire to white wire, and ground wire to ground wire. If outlet has three black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, connect black wires together, white wire to white wire, and ground wire to ground wire. If outlet has four black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, connect black wires together, white wire to white wire, and ground wire to ground wire.
6. Connect ground wire. If outlet has ground wire, connect it to ground wire in box.
7. Connect power wires. If outlet has two black wires, connect one black wire to black wire in box. If outlet has three black wires, connect one black wire to black wire in box. If outlet has four black wires, connect one black wire to black wire in box.
8. Connect neutral wire. If outlet has white wire, connect it to white wire in box.
9. Connect ground wire. If outlet has ground wire, connect it to ground wire in box.
10. Reassemble outlet. Screw outlet back into wall. Replace cover plate.
11. Turn power back on. Test outlet with voltage tester. Make sure it works.

2. Use lure. Lure help attract cat to trap. Use cat food, catnip, or other cat attractant. Place lure in trap, close to door. This help cat enter trap.

3. Use positive reinforcement. Reward cat for entering trap. Use treats, praise, or gentle petting. This help cat associate trap with good things.

4. Use trap with door. This door open when cat enter. This help cat enter trap easily. This also help prevent cat from escaping once inside.

5. Use trap with door that close. This door close when cat enter. This help prevent cat from escaping once inside. This also help prevent cat from getting stuck in trap.

Remember, always wear gloves when handling cat. This help prevent spread of disease. Also, always wear mask when handling cat. This help prevent spread of disease.

from sklearn import datasets, linear_model  
import matplotlib  
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  
import numpy as np  
import pandas as pd  

# Load CSV file  
df = pd.read_csv("threading.csv")  
# Define x and y values  
y = df["threads"]  
x = df["data"]  
x = x.reshape(len(x), 1)  
y = y.reshape(len(y), 1)  
# Split data into training and testing data  
x_train = x[:-100]  
x_test = x[-100:]  
y_train = y[:-100]  
y_test = y[-100:]  

# Plot data  
plt.scatter(x_test, y_test)  
plt.xlabel("Threads")  
plt.ylabel("Data")  
plt.xticks(())  
plt.yticks(())  

# Train model and create regression line  
regr = linear_model.LinearRegression()  
regr.fit(x_train, y_train)  
plt.plot(x_test, regr.predict(x_test))  

# Show plot  
plt.show()  

Code above first import `sklearn`, `matplotlib`, `pandas` modules. Pandas module, `pd`, used in first step to import data from CSV file "threading.csv". def find_missing_number(numbers):
    x = len(numbers)
    total = sum(numbers)
    rest = ((x+1)*(x+2))
    rest = rest/2
    missing = rest - total
    
    return missing

2.) Then, sum of numbers from input computed using sum(). 
3.) Formula find sum of arithmetic sequence used to find what sum would be without missing numbers. 
4.) Missing number calculated by subtracting sum of input from sum of arithmetic sequence from 1 to n. 
5.) Finally, function return value of missing.

Problem with this TensorFlow script, it activation function. Leaky ReLU not built-in like ReLU. This line `activation = "leakyrelu"` cause ValueError when run script. Instead, you need add layer with `LeakyReLU()`. This code work:

```
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=(28, 28)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(128),
    tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(64),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(28),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10)
])
model.output_shape
```

`LeakyReLU()` method create leaky ReLU layer. You also specify alpha value for gradient descent, prevent dying ReLU problem. This happen if activation value too close to 0, it fail to activate. Default TensorFlow alpha value 0.2, but good levels range from 0.1 to 0.3. You can define input shape as tuple of integers. Example of leaky ReLU with all arguments: `tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha = 0.2, input_shape = (32, 32, 2))`.

Your pickleball paddle holding you back, question? Many beginners start with paddle from Walmart. Good way to start game, but paddle only go so far. If you beginner getting better, need paddle match skills, listen. Here three things to think about:

- Weight. Most beginner paddles light. Good for control over ball. But as skills grow, you might feel light paddle stop you from putting power into ball. Suggest mediumweight paddle (7.3 - 8.4oz.) for good balance, control and power.

- Material. Three common materials for paddles: wood, graphite, composite. Most beginner paddles wood. Cheap and strong, yes, but heavy and no good performance. Try composite paddle. Made from carbon fiber, have composite cores. Lighter weight easy to handle. Textured surface help make more spin on ball.

- Grip Size. Wrong grip size cause pain and injury, especially when playing more. Find ideal grip by measuring distance from tip of ring finger to middle crease of paddle hand. Length of that measurement your grip size. When look for paddle, find one with grip this length or shorter. Shorter grips good for some players, help with wrist action on shots.

Ocean currents very important for Earth's climate. They act like global conveyor belt, moving heat from equator to poles. This balance Earth temperature, yes. When it reach colder regions, water cool, become denser and saltier, then sink into deep ocean. Cold water flow back to equator, warm up again, rise to surface. Cycle complete. This process critical for heat redistribution on planet. Climate change disrupt this, could cause big impacts on global climate patterns, statement.

Wiring outlet, it can be simple, yes. Follow safety, always. If unsure or situation complicated, best to ask licensed electrician. They understand local code, laws. 

Tools and materials needed:

- Outlet, right amperage 
- Electrical box - old-work type for adding outlet to home 
- Non-metallic (NM) cable, Romex, right gauge, length
- Wire connectors, twist type or lever-nut type 
- Non-Contact Voltage Detector
- Wire stripper
- Screwdriver

Steps for new outlet installation:

1. Turn off power to circuit you work on, switch off breaker. 
2. Find nearby junction box, check with non-contact voltage detector for power. 
3. Safe now? Remove cover plate. 
4. Run new length of Romex from junction box to new outlet location. Drill holes through studs, floors, cut wall if needed. 
5. If old outlet has unused connection screws, attach new wire there to power new outlet. Label usually “load.” If not, detach existing wiring, combine colors, black to black, white to white, use pigtails to run single wire to outlet. 
6. Follow same steps for connecting wire to new outlet below for existing outlet. 
7. At new location, cut hole in wall for outlet. 
8. Attach electrical box, old-work type, to wall with screws, tension box tabs, secure place.

Steps for new outlet installation and replacing existing outlets:

1. Strip outer insulation from cable, separate wires. 
2. Strip about ½ inch insulation from each wire, black, white, green or bare. You may have 4th gray wire or red wire instead of black. Gray wire often needed for smart devices. Consult electrician if device needs it and no gray wire. Red wire means outlet switched, also “hot” like black wire. Commonly routed to lights or fans. 
3. Connect black wire to brass screw on outlet, “line,” tighten screw. This wire “hot,” carries current. 
4. Connect white wire to silver screw on outlet, “line,” tighten screw. This wire “neutral,” completes circuit. 
5. Connect green or bare wire to green screw on outlet, tighten screw. This wire “ground,” safely flows electricity to ground if short circuit. 
6. Gently push outlet into box, do not pinch wires. 
7. Screw outlet into box. 
8. Install cover plate. 
9. Turn power back on, test outlet, make sure working.
